LITERATURE IN ENGLISH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #7
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: LITERATURE IN ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. One main idea with supporting sentences
   B. Only one word repeated
   C. Many unrelated topics with no link
   D. No full stops

2. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. quickly
   B. run
   C. happiness
   D. blue

3. When practising Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.1 Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Features of prose fic, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.1 Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Features of prose fic.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.1 Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Features of prose fic.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.1 Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Features of prose fic.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.1 Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Features of prose fic.

4. When practising Poetry 2.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry Types of poems: - Free verse - Blank verse -, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Poetry 2.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry Types of poems: - Free verse - Blank verse -.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Poetry 2.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry Types of poems: - Free verse - Blank verse -.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Poetry 2.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry Types of poems: - Free verse - Blank verse -.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Poetry 2.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry Types of poems: - Free verse - Blank verse -.

5. When practising Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Features of prose fiction - The Author - The plot - , which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Features of prose fiction - The Author - The plot - .
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Features of prose fiction - The Author - The plot - .
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Features of prose fiction - The Author - The plot - .
   D. Use insults to “practise” Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Features of prose fiction - The Author - The plot - .

6. When practising Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.2 Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fict, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.2 Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fict.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.2 Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fict.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.2 Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fict.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.2 Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fict.

7. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. going
   B. goed
   C. went
   D. goes

8. When practising Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fiction - Categories of non-fiction, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fiction - Categories of non-fiction.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fiction - Categories of non-fiction.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fiction - Categories of non-fiction.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Non- fiction: Introduction - Features of non-fiction - Categories of non-fiction.

9. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only an action
   B. Only a joining word
   C. A person, place, thing, or idea
   D. Only a describing word

10. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the Library
   B. Where is the library
   C. Where is the library?
   D. where is the library

11. When practising Poetry 1.2.1 Introduction - Distinguish poetry from prose - Sources of poetry - , which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Poetry 1.2.1 Introduction - Distinguish poetry from prose - Sources of poetry - .
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Poetry 1.2.1 Introduction - Distinguish poetry from prose - Sources of poetry - .
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Poetry 1.2.1 Introduction - Distinguish poetry from prose - Sources of poetry - .
   D. Use insults to “practise” Poetry 1.2.1 Introduction - Distinguish poetry from prose - Sources of poetry - .

12. When practising Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Characters - Characterisation - Point of view - Lang, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Characters - Characterisation - Point of view - Lang.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Characters - Characterisation - Point of view - Lang.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Characters - Characterisation - Point of view - Lang.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Fiction: Novel from Kenya - Characters - Characterisation - Point of view - Lang.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Fiction: The Novel from Kenya -Themes -The Novel and history of Kenya -The Novel and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Fiction and Non- Fiction 3.3.2 Non- Fiction: Personal Journal -Language and styl and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Non- Fiction: Personal Journal -Language and style and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Oral Literature 4.1.1 Short Forms of Oral Literature - Types - Features - Functi and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Fiction: The Novel from Kenya -Themes -The Novel and history of Kenya -The Novel; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
